taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Odufor, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 20.32 | 0.13606 | 0.13606
2 | 851.16 | 1.1039 | 1.2399
3 | 2511.9 | 15.803 | 17.043
4 | 1345 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

The layer resistivities are $\rho_1 = 20.32$, $\rho_2 = 851.16$, $\rho_3 = 2511.9$, and $\rho_4 = 1345$. Following the provided notation rules:
1. For the first group of three layers (1-2-3): $\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3$ ($20.32 < 851.16 < 2511.9$), which corresponds to the letter **A**.
2. For the second group of three layers (2-3-4): $\rho_2 < \rho_3 > \rho_4$ ($851.16 < 2511.9 > 1345$), which corresponds to the letter **K**.

Combining these, the correct notation for the 4-layer curve is **AK**. Since the letters are not the same, the single letter "A" is not a valid shorthand.

{"label_correct": false, "curve_type": "AK"}
